name: BackendBench
intro: BackendBench 是 Meta PyTorch 发布的开放评测套件，用于衡量模型或人类能否为 PyTorch 算子编写正确且高效的后端实现。它用 OpInfo 边界样例验证正确性，并用真实 Hugging Face 模型追踪得到的 TorchBench 张量形状评估性能。
build_method: OpInfo边界用例与真实模型张量追踪, 统一算子映射, 多测试套件执行验证
metric: Operator Correctness Pass Rate, Geometric Mean Speedup, Perf@p
task_type: 后端实现, 代码生成
eval_feature: 先正确性后性能, PyTorch eager参考实现, 真实模型形状, 全算子通过判定
scale: 271个OpInfo正确性算子, 124个性能算子; 平均13个OpInfo与110个TorchBench测试/算子
build_method_en: OpInfo edge cases and real-model tensor traces, unified operator mapping, multi-suite execution validation
eval_feature_en: Correctness before performance, PyTorch eager reference, real-model shapes, all-tests operator verdict
intro_en: BackendBench is an open Meta PyTorch evaluation suite for measuring whether models or humans can implement correct and fast PyTorch operator backends. It validates correctness with OpInfo edge cases and measures performance on TorchBench tensor shapes traced from real Hugging Face models.
scale_en: 271 OpInfo correctness operators, 124 performance operators; averages of 13 OpInfo and 110 TorchBench tests per operator
metric_en: Operator Correctness Pass Rate, Geometric Mean Speedup, Perf@p

drawio_review_note: BackendBench has no standalone benchmark paper. Reviewed against the official Meta PyTorch repository at fixed commit 2a8d7e19e2c13c789ff2dceb44883ea8ea04dab4, including README, docs/correctness.md, suite runners, CLI dispatch, and result aggregation. The diagram preserves the 271-operator OpInfo correctness set, 124-operator performance set, real Hugging Face model tensor traces, OpInfo edge cases, op_map alias coverage, torch.library dispatch, and the default five implementation attempts. At this fixed commit each CLI run chooses exactly one mutually exclusive --suite among Smoke, OpInfo, FACTO, and TorchBench; Smoke does not fan out into the other suites, and OpInfo/FACTO correctness reports remain partitioned. Within the selected TorchBench suite, suite-local correctness[] and performance[] entries are paired by the same test index before aggregation. Correctness uses PyTorch-reference comparison with equal_nan and 1e-2 tolerances; performance uses synchronized triton.do_bench timing. The performance geometric mean is not correctness-gated and assigns failed implementations 1x, while Perf@p alone requires correctness and speedup > p. No score is merged across suites.
